items.title: FPL GW10 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 10 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: Gabriel and Calafiori lead a Gameweek 10 defensive transfer rush
items.summary:
Arsenal defenders are the standout Gameweek 10 targets ahead of Hull at home, with a 57% projected clean-sheet chance making their defence the week’s clearest source of points. Gabriel is the preferred long-term buy because he combines defensive-contribution potential, bonus appeal and set-piece threat, while Riccardo Calafiori is also a strong immediate pick due to his advanced positioning in dominant Arsenal matches. Owners should keep Calafiori, and can even consider him as a high-upside captaincy differential. Cristhian Mosquera is useful in the short term but is not viewed as a secure long-term route into Arsenal’s defence: William Saliba’s return is expected to threaten his centre-back role, while potential minutes at right-back would be less reliable.

Bournemouth’s Silva is the other elite defensive buy. He has the league’s best defensive-contribution record among defenders, Bournemouth are producing repeated clean sheets, and their next three fixtures are favourable. Brighton’s De Cuyper and Spurs’ Vuskovic are strong longer-term options but can wait a week because their Gameweek 10 meeting with Brentford is not the ideal entry point. Nottingham Forest defenders, including Neco Williams, should be sold before a difficult run, while Manchester City’s Gvardiol and Newcastle’s Hall are expendable rather than urgent sales. Everton’s Tarkowski is worth keeping for Coventry, but his poor fixtures afterwards make him a short-term hold rather than a transfer target.

Up front, Erling Haaland remains the priority buy and the leading captain for Forest, Fulham and Leeds, despite a Gameweek 9 blank, as his chance volume remains excellent. Liverpool’s Isak is also a buy for a long favourable fixture run and could inherit penalties if Mohamed Salah is absent. Nicolas Jackson is recommended on form and for fixtures against Manchester United, Sunderland and Ipswich, while Evanilson becomes a serious watch after improving shot and expected-goal numbers ahead of Ipswich; early substitutions and possible competition from Kroopy are the caveats. Existing owners should retain Alexander Isak, Barry and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, while Brobby, Whistler and Emerson are sales due to poor attacking output, fixtures or minutes.

In midfield, Tavernier is the preferred Gameweek 10 signing for Ipswich away, with Bournemouth’s long fixture run and his tendency to arrive for high-quality chances outweighing his low shot volume. Rogers and Manzambi also offer value, while Gakpo is a viable Liverpool differential if his recent minutes remain secure. Keep Martin Odegaard for Hull at home because Arsenal should dominate and he retains penalty upside when Gyokeres is off the pitch; Pascal Gross is a hold for upcoming Hull and Newcastle fixtures, and Mbeumo is worth one final start against Aston Villa before a likely exit. Sell Saka because of his extended injury absence, and move on from Cherki due to persistent rotation. Palmer is a hold rather than a priority purchase: his penalty in Gameweek 9 does not offset weak underlying data and a high price.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Nottingham Forest; he remains the standout captain through home fixtures against Fulham and Leeds.
Buy Gabriel first among Arsenal defenders for long-term security, then consider Calafiori for Hull at home and his attacking upside.
Silva is the preferred Bournemouth defender thanks to exceptional defensive-contribution reliability, clean-sheet form and a strong fixture run.
Keep Mosquera only as a short-term Arsenal option, with Saliba’s return expected to reduce his security of starts from around Gameweek 12.
Target Tavernier in midfield for Ipswich away, while Rogers and Manzambi are cheaper alternatives with favourable schedules.
Keep Odegaard for Hull at home and hold Mbeumo for Aston Villa, but consider selling Mbeumo after Gameweek 10.
Sell Nottingham Forest defenders, Cherki and injured Saka; Tarkowski is only a one-week hold for Coventry.
Monitor Evanilson for Ipswich after improved underlying numbers, but factor in early substitutions and possible competition for minutes.

items.title: 12 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 10 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Saka’s form and Arsenal’s defence headline Gameweek 10 plans
items.summary:
Bukayo Saka becomes the standout FPL option after reaching six attacking returns and moving to the top of the overall scoring charts. Arsenal’s defence also remains comfortably the league’s best, making their home fixture against Crystal Palace an appealing clean-sheet opportunity. William Saliba may return soon, however, so managers investing in Arsenal defenders need to weigh immediate security against the possibility of selection changes.

João Pedro is expected to miss out until after the international break. Managers with adequate bench cover can consider holding him for one more week rather than selling at a loss, but he is a clear transfer out for sides that need an active starter. Rayan Cherki is also a sell after another benching, while Morgan Gibbs-White is a reasonable hold despite no attacking return since Gameweek 4, particularly for managers who do not need the funds elsewhere. Nicolas Jackson, with five goals in eight starts, and Evanilson, who has returned in four consecutive gameweeks, offer the more convincing forward form.

Liverpool’s fixture run improves now that the Arsenal match is behind them, putting Cody Gakpo, Virgil van Dijk and Alexander Isak on the watchlist. Bournemouth are also building defensive momentum with three straight clean sheets, and Marcos Senesi has delivered eight points in each of those matches. Pascal Groß and Thiago sit one booking from suspension on four yellow cards, while Kepa, Silva, Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are among the popular assets on three cautions. Manzambi continues to return but is repeatedly substituted early, creating a minutes risk that managers should monitor before buying.
key_points: Bukayo Saka has six attacking returns and is the game’s highest-scoring player ahead of Arsenal’s home match with Crystal Palace.
Arsenal remain the league’s strongest defence, although a possible William Saliba return could affect defensive selections.
João Pedro is likely unavailable until after the international break; hold only if bench cover is sufficient, otherwise sell.
Rayan Cherki is a recommended sale after another benching, while Morgan Gibbs-White remains a viable hold if cash is not needed.
Nicolas Jackson has five goals in eight starts and Evanilson has returned in each of the last four gameweeks.
Liverpool’s improved fixtures raise the appeal of Cody Gakpo, Virgil van Dijk and Alexander Isak.
Bournemouth have three consecutive clean sheets, with Marcos Senesi scoring eight points in each of them.
Pascal Groß and Thiago are one yellow card from suspension, while Kepa, Silva, Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are on three bookings.

items.headline: Haaland captaincy and a Gibbs-White-to-Semenyo move headline Gameweek 10 plans
items.summary:
The preferred Gameweek 10 approach is to captain Erling Haaland and roll the transfer, preserving two free transfers for after the international break. Despite a squad that still carries several problems and relies on a 4-4-2 because of a weak bench, it produces a green arrow in Gameweek 9, so there is little appetite to force a move before the break.

João Pedro remains in the squad despite his price drop. The hope is that he returns after the international break, when his reduced ownership could make him a useful differential. The bench options, including Bobby Thomas and Slater, offer little immediate help, which makes holding rather than selling Pedro a calculated risk: it sacrifices team value but could avoid needing to buy him back if he regains fitness and form.

Morgan Gibbs-White is the biggest transfer concern, with Cole Palmer also under scrutiny. There are several midfield targets, including Manchester United options after their encouraging spell against Chelsea before the red card, but Bournemouth’s fixtures make their midfielders the clearest short-term targets. Antoine Semenyo is particularly appealing now that he is back available for Ipswich away in Gameweek 10, while Marcus Tavernier and Ryan Christie are alternative routes into Bournemouth’s attack.

If injuries or other problems force action, the aggressive option is a minus-four: Gibbs-White to Tavernier and a defensive upgrade to a Bournemouth player, doubling up on their favourable run. That move offers immediate fixture upside but costs points and reduces flexibility, so the stronger plan is to avoid the hit, trust Haaland with the armband and enter the international break with two free transfers.
key_points: Captain Erling Haaland in Gameweek 10, with rolling the transfer the preferred move.
João Pedro is held through his price fall in the hope that he returns after the international break as a low-owned differential.
Morgan Gibbs-White is the leading sell candidate, while Cole Palmer is also a concern for future transfers.
Antoine Semenyo is a prime target for Bournemouth’s Ipswich away fixture now that he is available again.
Marcus Tavernier and Ryan Christie are alternative Bournemouth midfield options for Gameweek 10.
A forced minus-four could fund Gibbs-White to Tavernier plus a Bournemouth defensive upgrade, but it is viewed as less attractive than banking a transfer.
The 4-4-2 setup is largely dictated by weak bench options, including Bobby Thomas and Slater.

items.headline: Raya move completes Arsenal defensive triple-up as defenders dominate FPL planning
items.summary:
Mark heads into Gameweek 10 with one free transfer, £1.8m in the bank and a clear priority: replace Kinsky with Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya. The move, planned for several weeks, creates a triple Arsenal defence alongside Calafiori and Conor ahead of Hull City at home. Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential, DefCon scoring and bonus upside make the defensive triple-up attractive despite the risk of rotation around Calafiori and Conor when Saliba returns. Mark is willing to make the transfer early if price changes threaten the move, as his budget leaves no margin.

Erling Haaland is the likely captain away to Nottingham Forest, largely because Mark does not own Liverpool forward Alexander Isak. Isak, away to a struggling Crystal Palace side, is considered arguably the strongest Gameweek 10 captain on form and fixture, while Chelsea attackers also appeal at Sunderland. Haaland remains the default choice for Mark and looks even stronger in Gameweek 11 at home to Fulham, but captaincy is unusually open in the coming weeks: Isak’s fixtures from Gameweek 11, including Manchester United, Everton, Sunderland and Leeds, make him a major future target.

Nicolas Jackson is not viewed as a short-term stand-in for the injured Joao Pedro. His Aston Villa run — Manchester United away, Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home and Crystal Palace at home — is strong enough to justify holding him for roughly six weeks. If Pedro returns, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is more likely to make way, although Calvert-Lewin remains useful as a home-fixture rotation forward. Morgan Gibbs-White is the next likely sale, with cheaper midfielders such as Manzambi or Tavernier able to release funds for Pedro, Isak or defensive upgrades.

The central strategic theme is to lean into defenders rather than force traditional 3-4-3 or 3-5-2 structures. Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma replacement, Diper, Tottenham’s Van Hecke and Vuskovic, Leeds’ Moravcik, Bournemouth’s Silva, Liverpool’s Jack and Arsenal’s Gabriel all offer a combination of clean-sheet potential, DefCon points, bonus and set-piece threat. Gabriel is especially appealing on a wildcard because his secure minutes distinguish him from Calafiori and Conor, while Diper’s attacking numbers — two goals, four assists and three double-digit returns — make him close to essential despite concerns over Mitoma’s eventual return. A five-defender formation is increasingly viable, with DefCon defenders preferred even as first substitutes over cheap attacking enablers.
key_points: Mark plans to transfer Kinsky to David Raya in Gameweek 10, completing a Raya-Calafiori-Conor Arsenal defensive triple-up for Hull City at home.
Haaland is Mark’s captain away to Nottingham Forest, although Isak at Crystal Palace is viewed as the leading alternative for managers who own him.
Jackson remains a medium-term hold because Aston Villa’s fixtures stay strong through Gameweeks 11-15, so Joao Pedro is not an automatic replacement when fit.
Gibbs-White is the likely next player sold, with Manzambi or Tavernier possible cheaper replacements to fund future moves.
Isak becomes a key transfer or wildcard target from Gameweek 11 due to Liverpool’s favourable run, especially Manchester United, Everton, Sunderland and Leeds.
Gabriel offers the safest Arsenal defensive route thanks to secure starts, while Calafiori and Conor carry greater rotation risk.
Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Moravcik, Silva, Jack and Diper are highlighted as high-upside DefCon defenders, making 5-3-2 or 5-2-3 increasingly attractive.
Diper is backed to retain his Brighton role despite Mitoma’s return from injury, having already produced two goals, four assists and three double-digit hauls.

items.title: FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW10 ✅
items.headline: Gabriel edges Haaland as Gameweek 10’s standout captaincy pick
items.summary:
Arsenal’s home meeting with Hull makes their defence the defining Gameweek 10 investment. David Raya has the best projected goalkeeper score and Arsenal’s clean-sheet odds are expected to approach 60%, while Gabriel is the leading captaincy option on the projections at 6.3 points, narrowly ahead of Erling Haaland. Gabriel’s secure minutes, set-piece threat and potential defensive-contribution points make him the only Arsenal defender worth serious captaincy consideration; Raya is preferred in goal, but his ceiling is lower. Triple Arsenal defence is viable for a one-week Free Hit, although full-back options such as Jurrien Timber and Riccardo Calafiori carry rotation risk depending on Champions League minutes.

For longer-term goalkeeper value, Bart Verbruggen and Djordje Petrovic are preferred budget alternatives to the premium options, while Tottenham’s improving form also puts Guglielmo Vicario in contention. Bournemouth are highlighted as an emerging defensive source: their expected-goals-conceded record is among the league’s best, and defenders such as Milos Kerkez, Marcos Senesi and Illia Zabarnyi offer clean-sheet potential alongside defensive-contribution returns. Cheap defenders Dara O’Shea, Charlie Taylor and Mendy are useful bench options, with Taylor particularly appealing if his injury proves minor.

In midfield, Martin Odegaard is the preferred Arsenal attacker over Noni Madueke because he has corners, some free-kick and penalty potential while Bukayo Saka is absent, plus strong underlying numbers. However, Arsenal slots may be better spent in defence for steadier returns. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are excellent buys after scoring against Manchester United, while Bournemouth’s Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier offer upside against Ipswich. Tavernier has five goals, but Kluivert’s recent shot volume is stronger. At lower prices, Crysencio Summerville is producing, but Matt Ruedoni is the standout fifth-midfield option: he is back to full fitness, has scored in three of four games, appears to have penalties and set pieces, and has playable fixtures against Everton, Palace, Leeds and Ipswich.

Up front, Haaland remains the top forward projection, but Alexander Isak is a premium alternative against a Crystal Palace side rated worst for expected goals conceded. Barry is identified as the best budget striker at £5.6m, with enough value to start or bench depending on fixtures. Kai Havertz is avoided despite a strong projection because his minutes are uncertain and Arsenal have alternatives. Evanilson is favoured marginally over Dominic Calvert-Lewin thanks to Bournemouth’s form and a long favourable fixture run, though Calvert-Lewin’s home fixtures from Gameweek 12 are also attractive. A projected best XI includes Pickford, Kerkez, Gabriel, Tarkowski, Palmer, Madueke, Mbeumo, Odegaard, Barry, Calvert-Lewin and Haaland.
key_points: Captain Gabriel against Hull if backing Arsenal’s exceptional clean-sheet probability; he marginally outscores Haaland in the Gameweek 10 projections.
Raya is the preferred goalkeeper for Gameweek 10, while Verbruggen or Petrovic offer better longer-term budget value.
Avoid relying on Arsenal full-backs for captaincy or transfers until Champions League selection clarifies the rotation risk around Timber and Calafiori.
Consider Bournemouth defenders and attackers: their defensive numbers are strong, while Kluivert and Tavernier both appeal for the Ipswich fixture.
Odegaard is the best Arsenal midfield buy if choosing one, but Arsenal defensive slots are considered more reliable while Saka is out.
Ruedoni at £4.9m is the preferred cheap fifth midfielder due to improving minutes, penalties and a favourable four-match run.
Barry is the leading budget forward, while Evanilson is slightly preferred to Calvert-Lewin for sustained startability over the coming fixtures.
A Gameweek 10 Free Hit can justify Raya, Calafiori and Gabriel together, with Gabriel captain, rather than using Arsenal slots on Odegaard or Madueke.

items.title: Is it time to sell Gibbs-White? 🤔 FPL GW10 Early Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Hold Morgan Gibbs-White and prioritise rolling transfers before Gameweek 10
items.summary:
Morgan Gibbs-White remains a hold despite no attacking return since Gameweek 4. His 90-minute security, occasional penalty potential and acceptable upcoming schedule — Bournemouth away in Gameweek 11, Chelsea at home in Gameweek 12 and Hull in Gameweek 13 — outweigh the frustration of facing Manchester City this week. Managers who do not want to start him can bench him, while the international break makes preserving a transfer especially valuable. Tavernier is the preferred cheaper replacement if funds are needed, but Gibbs-White is not a forced sale.

Ryan Chery is much closer to a sell because his minutes have become unreliable. Repeated early substitutions, bench appearances and the likelihood of a Champions League start make him difficult to trust for Gameweek 10, even if he starts against Forest. Tavernier, at £6.6m with Ipswich away followed by Forest, Fulham, Brighton and Hull, is the standout budget-midfield purchase. Morgan Rogers is the preferred mid-priced alternative because of good underlying numbers, favourable fixtures through Gameweek 13 and no European rotation, while Mbeumo is still viable but is more attractive from Gameweek 12 after Liverpool away. Gross is worth delaying until Gameweek 11 because he is one yellow card from a suspension, and Manzambi's regular early substitutions make him less appealing despite recent returns.

Arsenal defender Conza offers huge short-term appeal against Hull at home after returns of 10, 14 and nine points, but his longer-term minutes become a concern once Celibra returns from injury, likely after the international break. Conza may still play across league, Europe and cups, yet potential cameos and rotation with Celibra, Ben White and Timber make him a risk for a new buyer. Existing owners should keep him until the problem materialises, but non-owners can reasonably avoid him and choose more secure defenders such as Silva, Vuskovic or Muramovic. Brighton's Maxim Diper is the more tempting aggressive buy: he plays at left wing while classified as a defender, has Brentford at home next, and his threat from returning players such as Minte and Mitoma appears less immediate. Vuskovic is a safer Brighton defensive alternative with Defcon and goal threat.

Up front, Evan Nielson is a strong Gameweek 10 purchase for Ipswich but has benefited from some fortunate recent goals. Nicolas Jackson is the preferred medium-term forward because Villa's Gameweeks 11-15 schedule is exceptional: Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home, Palace at home and Coventry away. Joao Pedro is unlikely to feature against Sunderland, but managers who held him through Gameweek 9 can consider keeping him through the international break if they can field a strong XI, hoping for a return against Leeds in Gameweek 11. With three free transfers and £1.9m in the bank, the current squad is set to roll: Haaland is the likely captain, with Arsenal's triple defence against Hull, Diper against Brentford, and a midfield of Palmer, Rogers, Mbeumo and Gross all strong enough to avoid unnecessary moves.
key_points: Morgan Gibbs-White is a hold rather than a must-sell; bench him against Manchester City if necessary and reassess after the international break.
Tavernier is the preferred cheap midfield transfer at £6.6m, with Ipswich away in Gameweek 10 and a strong run thereafter.
Ryan Chery is a sell due to consistently poor minutes and a high risk of further rotation after European football.
Conza is an excellent one-week Arsenal pick against Hull, but Celibra's expected return after the break creates a serious Gameweek 11-onwards minutes risk.
Maxim Diper is favoured over Conza for new buyers because he is effectively playing left wing for Brighton and has a favourable fixture run.
Delay buying Gross until Gameweek 11 if possible, as he sits on four yellow cards and could miss Hull if booked against Brentford.
Evan Nielson is attractive for Ipswich in Gameweek 10, but Jackson is preferred for Villa's outstanding Gameweeks 11-15 fixtures.
Haaland is the current captain choice, while rolling a third free transfer to reach four after the international break is the preferred team plan.

items.title: The *NEW FPL META* Changes EVERYTHING... (My GW10 Transfer Plans)
items.headline: Defenders drive FPL returns as five-at-the-back enters the Gameweek 10 debate
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 reinforces the case for prioritising high-upside defenders. Nine of the top 20 FPL scorers are defenders, with clean sheets, defensive-contribution points, bonus and set-piece threat producing both dependable floors and explosive hauls. The preferred profile is a defender with clean-sheet potential, DefCon appeal and aerial or attacking threat: Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi/Silva, Arsenal’s Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori, Tottenham’s Micky van de Ven, Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa, Leeds’ Jaka Bijol/Muharremovic and Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma-type attacking full-back options are all cited in the wider pool. Van Hecke’s 15-point Gameweek 9 haul illustrates how decisive these picks are becoming.

For Gameweek 10, the plan is to consider four or even five defenders rather than automatically starting underperforming midfielders. Sharda is the clearest bench or sell candidate after another low-threat display, while Gross has no shots across his past two matches and may no longer merit an automatic start despite set pieces and penalties. Palmer is also under scrutiny: his return against Manchester United comes from a penalty and his wider open-play output remains unconvincing. Bryan Mbeumo, by contrast, remains a hold despite a blank because he creates multiple high-quality chances and threatens goal himself; Aston Villa’s high line makes him particularly appealing in Gameweek 10.

The defensive approach remains fixture-sensitive rather than blindly committed to five at the back. Muharremovic is worth benching away to Chelsea in Gameweek 11, while bad fixtures can justify moving back to three or four defenders. Tottenham’s defence still appeals after the Crystal Palace clean sheet, but their attack does not: Spurs generate 3.58 xG against 10 men yet score only twice, so the result should not trigger major attacking investment. Bournemouth continue to demand attention after another win and clean sheet, with Ipswich next, while Nottingham Forest assets such as Morgan Gibbs-White look sellable as their poor finishing and defensive underperformance continue.

Looking ahead, two saved transfers for Gameweek 11 could fund Calafiori or Konsa to Luka Vuskovic, depending on minutes security, plus Sharda to Manzambi ahead of Sunderland at home. Vuskovic is valued for the same clean-sheet, DefCon and set-piece formula, while Van Hecke is another longer-term target. Mbeumo becomes more attractive from Gameweek 12-13 as his fixtures improve. Chelsea’s tougher run from Gameweek 14, featuring Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa, could make Palmer a route to Gabriel or another premium defender, with Bournemouth attackers such as Kroupi, if his minutes grow after the international break, among possible midfield replacements.
key_points: Start four defenders in Gameweek 10 as the preferred baseline, with five at the back a viable option if all defensive fixtures are favourable.
Bench or sell Sharda after repeated low-threat performances; Gross is also no longer an automatic starter after recording no shots in his last two matches.
Hold Mbeumo despite his blank because his chance creation and shooting remain strong, and Aston Villa’s high line improves his Gameweek 10 appeal.
Do not overreact to Tottenham’s 2-0 win over 10-man Crystal Palace: their defence remains useful, but their attack still underdelivers against expected goals.
Bournemouth defensive assets remain priority picks after a sixth straight clean sheet, with Ipswich next on the schedule.
Consider Gibbs-White a sell as Nottingham Forest continue to underperform at both ends despite respectable underlying numbers.
Target Vuskovic in Gameweek 11, potentially replacing Calafiori or Konsa, and pair the move with Sharda to Manzambi if minutes and fixtures align.
Palmer is a possible later sale ahead of Chelsea’s difficult Gameweek 14 fixture run, potentially freeing funds for Gabriel and a stronger defensive core.

items.title: FPL Kneejerk Gameweek 10 🔥 Green arrow ✅ Bournemouth players in 🤔
items.headline: Arsenal defenders emerge as bold Gameweek 10 captaincy alternatives to Haaland
items.summary:
Gameweek 10 looks far calmer than the previous round, with many squads already well set and little need to force transfers before the international break. The preferred approach is to preserve transfers unless there is a genuine minutes concern or a clear structural upgrade, particularly in defence. The view is that several popular assets — including Morgan Gibbs-White, Pascal Gross, Jorgen Strand Larsen and the Bournemouth midfield options — remain perfectly playable rather than urgent sales, even where recent returns disappoint.

Arsenal’s defence is the standout asset group for Hull at home. Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori and Cristhian Mosquera are all considered strong starters, with Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential high even after a difficult match against Liverpool. Calafiori completing 90 minutes increases the chance that he is rested in Europe and starts in Gameweek 10. Arsenal defenders are legitimate captaincy options, although Erling Haaland remains the leading choice, polling comfortably ahead of them. Alexander Isak is a viable differential captain against Crystal Palace, while Kai Havertz is not especially attractive because of his forward slot and uncertainty over his longer-term appeal.

The main strategic trend is towards investing in defence and selecting the best weekly XI rather than forcing expensive attackers in and out. Players such as Luka Vuskovic, Micky van de Ven, Jan Paul van Hecke, Murillo, Silva and the Arsenal defenders are discussed as attractive defensive options, especially for their defensive-contribution potential. Lewis Hall is likely to be sold once a defensive transfer is needed, but not necessarily immediately: Newcastle’s upcoming schedule and the strength of the current squad mean a luxury move is hard to justify. Konza/Mosquera is worth holding while William Saliba remains absent, but his role becomes much less secure once Saliba returns, even if he continues to receive substantial minutes across competitions.

There are significant benching headaches because many attackers have favourable fixtures. Barry, with Coventry at home, is viewed as an automatic starter, while Gross at home and on penalties is also difficult to bench. Calvert-Lewin is preferred to defenders such as Van Hecke when he has a home fixture, and Manzambi is generally the player to bench in close calls because of his recurring early substitutions despite recent returns. The advice is not to overreact to one-week bench points or force a Bench Boost unless the entire bench is genuinely strong and unlikely to improve later.

Free Hit planning remains flexible, with Gameweeks 12, 14 and 15 all plausible. Gameweek 14 is particularly appealing as a way to temporarily remove Chelsea and Liverpool assets facing each other, while loading up on Manchester United players for Coventry at home, plus Bournemouth options against Hull. The key principle is to buy Liverpool players ahead of their strong longer-term fixture run rather than waiting to Free Hit them in for one good match; the Free Hit should instead target short-term players, such as Manchester United assets, who are not wanted afterwards.
key_points: Haaland is the leading Gameweek 10 captain, but Gabriel, Calafiori or another Arsenal defender against Hull are credible high-upside alternatives.
Do not rush to sell Gibbs-White before Manchester City; he is nailed for 90 minutes, on penalties and has useful fixtures later in the season.
Start Barry against Coventry at home regardless of his performance in the preceding match, as the fixture and expected minutes are too good to bench.
Gross remains a strong hold because Brighton’s fixtures are favourable and he has penalties, though he sits one yellow card from suspension.
Prioritise defensive transfers such as Vuskovic, Silva, Murillo, Van Hecke or Arsenal defenders rather than forcing attacker changes.
Hold Konza/Mosquera for now if already owned, but monitor Saliba’s return because it could damage his Premier League security.
Avoid buying defence solely to bench a playable attacker; Lewis Hall to a premium defensive option is viewed as a luxury move in Gameweek 10.
Gameweek 14 Free Hit is a possible route to target Manchester United against Coventry while temporarily removing Chelsea and Liverpool players.

items.title: MY FPL GW10 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 GABRIEL vs BOURNEMOUTH PLAYERS 🍒 Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Gibbs-White is the priority sale, but rolling before the break may beat chasing Bournemouth points
items.summary:
Gameweek 10 leaves the squad short of depth despite a fortunate Gameweek 9 green arrow, driven by Van Hecke’s 15 points and De Cuyper’s nine points from the bench. Haaland is the likely captain, with Morgan Rogers holding the vice-captaincy for Aston Villa’s trip to Sunderland, while David Raya and Riccardo Calafiori are retained in an Arsenal defensive double-up. Van Hecke starts against Spurs because Bobby Thomas is flagged, Joao Pedro is unavailable and Slater offers little bench cover; his attacking threat also makes him playable despite Leeds being stronger at home.

Joao Pedro is expected to miss Chelsea’s Gameweek 10 trip to Sunderland, but is worth holding for now. Having already carried him through Gameweek 9, selling before the international break is judged premature if he can return in Gameweek 11, particularly as sales could make him a useful differential. The bigger concerns are Morgan Gibbs-White and Cole Palmer. Gibbs-White remains a regular 90-minute penalty taker, but Nottingham Forest are struggling for goals and his creative output depends on unreliable finishers. Palmer is capable of explosive returns but does not look worth £9.8m, especially with Chelsea less convincing away from home and noticeably weaker without Joao Pedro.

The leading transfer target is a Bournemouth midfielder ahead of the trip to Ipswich. Marcus Tavernier is the safest, most nailed long-term choice, with set pieces and proven FPL pedigree, while Ryan offers cheaper access at £6.3m and stronger shot volume. Rayan Cherki is viewed as potentially Bournemouth’s best midfield asset but remains a minutes risk after his substitute appearance, making Gameweek 11 a safer entry point. Antoine Semenyo is avoided because his sub-70-minute outings and European schedule threaten his minutes, while Bryan Mbeumo is one to monitor for Manchester United’s better fixture run from Gameweek 12.

The preferred plan is to roll the transfer and enter the international break with two free moves, protecting against injuries and allowing more flexibility to sell Palmer or Gibbs-White later. If a move becomes necessary because Calafiori appears unlikely to start after Champions League involvement, Gabriel is the premium replacement, although funding him likely requires Palmer to Tavernier. The most realistic one-transfer move is Gibbs-White to Tavernier. A more aggressive -4 is Gibbs-White to Tavernier plus Bobby Thomas to Bournemouth defender Antonio Silva, strengthening a defence where reliable returns from Gabriel, Van Hecke, De Cuyper and Silva currently look more attractive than chasing cheap midfielders.
key_points: Haaland is the expected Gameweek 10 captain, with Morgan Rogers vice-captain away at Sunderland.
Hold Joao Pedro through his likely Gameweek 10 absence unless Chelsea confirm a longer lay-off after the international break.
Morgan Gibbs-White is the main transfer concern, with Nottingham Forest’s poor attack undermining his otherwise solid underlying involvement.
Marcus Tavernier is the preferred Bournemouth midfielder for a direct Gibbs-White replacement; Ryan is a cheaper, higher-shot-volume alternative.
Rayan Cherki is attractive but carries a Gameweek 10 start and fitness risk, so waiting until Gameweek 11 is favoured.
Rolling the transfer is the current preferred strategy, preserving two free moves through an injury-prone international break.
If making a -4, Gibbs-White to Tavernier and Bobby Thomas to Antonio Silva is the preferred defensive upgrade.
Monitor Riccardo Calafiori’s Champions League minutes: if he looks at risk of missing Hull, Gabriel becomes the high-upside Arsenal replacement.

items.title: FPL GW10 TRANSFER PLANS ✅ MY GAMEWEEK 10 TEAM 🎯
items.headline: Haaland retains captaincy as rolling a transfer protects flexibility before the international break
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the preferred captain for Gameweek 10 despite a blank against Brighton, with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers close alternatives because Chelsea face Sunderland. Haaland’s record of scoring in seven straight matches before that blank gives him the consistency edge when the captaincy call is tight. Palmer is a clear hold after scoring a penalty against Manchester United and creating further chances, while Rogers is favoured over Bruno Fernandes among midfield options. Chelsea’s Estêvão impresses but is not considered reliable enough for minutes.

The proposed XI is Raya; Konsa, Marcos Silva, De Cuyper and Van Hecke; Bryan Mbeumo, Palmer, Rogers and Pascal Groß; Barry and Haaland. João Pedro, Schade and Mendy are on the bench. The closest selection call is Van Hecke versus Schade: Schade offers attacking upside but has uncertain minutes amid competition from Dango and Antony, while Van Hecke has Leeds next and Spurs’ strong defensive run continues. Van Hecke’s 15-point haul is not viewed as a reason to chase him blindly, although Spurs have Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham in the next four.

Bournemouth defenders are the main long-term defensive targets. Marcos Silva and Hill combine clean-sheet potential with strong defensive-contribution numbers, while Vaskovic and Muharemovic offer similar appeal at value prices. Bournemouth have gone six games without conceding in all competitions and have Ipswich next; Evanilson is also attractive at £6.4m after four goals in four games and an overall return of four goals and four assists in nine. Arsenal, Forest, Liverpool, Bournemouth and Spurs rate as the league’s best defences by expected goals conceded, with Arsenal’s home match against Hull offering an elite clean-sheet opportunity.

The preferred transfer strategy is to roll one free transfer and enter the final international break of the year with two. Mendy to Vlasic would improve the starting team, but it uses most of the £1.3m in the bank and is not a decisive upgrade on starting Van Hecke against Leeds. Keeping cash available matters because Konsa or De Cuyper may later need replacing, and the longer-term aim is to move towards Gabriel. João Pedro to Dominic Calvert-Lewin is also considered, particularly with Calvert-Lewin’s home form and Coventry at home in Gameweek 12, but can wait until after the break. European midweek fixtures add another reason not to make an early move.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 10, with Palmer and Rogers the nearest alternatives because Chelsea play Sunderland.
Roll the transfer rather than buying Vlasic or Calvert-Lewin immediately, taking two free transfers into the international break.
Start Van Hecke narrowly over Schade, although Schade’s attacking upside makes it a close call.
Keep Palmer despite missed chances against Manchester United; Sunderland next makes him a strong hold.
Target Bournemouth defenders Silva and Hill, plus Vaskovic or Muharemovic, for clean sheets and defensive-contribution returns.
Evanilson is a £6.4m forward option after scoring in four consecutive matches, with Ipswich next.
Avoid buying Estêvão despite his performance for Chelsea, as his starting minutes remain insecure.
Monitor De Cuyper and Konsa for future rotation risk, with Gabriel the intended premium defensive upgrade.

items.title: BENCH BOOST DRAFT! 🚀 | FPL CHAI'S GW10 TEAM SELECTION | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Gabriel captaincy emerges as the Gameweek 10 upside play against Hull
items.summary:
Gameweek 10 presents a strong captaincy case for Arsenal defender Gabriel at home to Hull, even with Erling Haaland retaining the safer default appeal away to Nottingham Forest. Gabriel is viewed as the most secure starter in Arsenal’s defence, with Hull likely to concede corners and aerial opportunities, while his clean-sheet, defensive-contribution and set-piece potential offers genuine double-digit upside. Haaland remains a sensible captain after a rare blank against Brighton, but Forest have proved capable of frustrating leading sides under Oliver Glasner.

Josh is set to Bench Boost in Gameweek 10, with Kinsky, Gabriel, Lewis Hall, Micky van de Ven, Calafiori, Harvey Barnes, Pascal Gross, Morgan Rogers, Kevin Schade, Haaland and Nicolas Jackson in his XI, plus Bernd Leno, Charalampos Kostoulas, Morgan Gibbs-White and Dango Ouattara on the bench. The chip is driven by two active goalkeepers with reasonable fixtures, a strong playing bench and a desire to stop leaving returns unused. The principal risks are Calafiori’s place against Hull and the minutes of Kostoulas and Schade, so a four-point hit remains possible if it improves the Bench Boost squad.

The preferred transfer route is Schade to a Bournemouth midfielder, with Ryan Christie, Marcus Tavernier and Dango Ouattara among the options, while Calafiori to Bournemouth defender Marcos Senesi is also considered. Bournemouth’s trip to Ipswich is attractive, and Senesi offers clean-sheet prospects, defensive contributions and set-piece threat. Gibbs-White is frustrating after continued underlying involvement without returns, but his reliable 90-minute role makes him harder to sell before a Bench Boost, particularly with Forest capable of producing big-game performances.

Tottenham assets are increasingly relevant after three consecutive wins. Mohammed Kudus looks a compelling midfield differential after returning against Crystal Palace and producing encouraging minutes, while Kinsky and Van de Ven are viable defensive holds. Spurs away at Leeds is not regarded as the ideal entry point, but the subsequent Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham fixtures could make a Spurs attacker desirable from Gameweek 11. Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Kostoulas remain quality options despite City limiting their output, while Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson is a strong longer-term pick despite concerns over fatigue and an awkward Gameweek 10 trip to Manchester United.

The contrarian calls for Gameweek 10 are that Jackson could disappoint at Old Trafford, with Manchester United expected to respond in Michael Carrick’s final match before the international break, and that Tavernier may be overbought after recent returns before Bournemouth face a potentially deep Ipswich block. Differential attacking selections include Bradley Barcola or Alexander Isak away to Crystal Palace, while Eberechi Eze is backed to exploit Arsenal’s injury issues against Hull. Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Lewis Hall are identified as lower-owned defensive alternatives, and Barry becomes a more appealing forward option if fit for Coventry at home.
key_points: Captain Gabriel against Hull for set-piece, clean-sheet and defensive-contribution upside; Haaland away to Nottingham Forest remains the safer alternative.
Josh plans to Bench Boost in Gameweek 10, with Leno, Kostoulas, Gibbs-White and Ouattara currently forming a playable bench.
Schade to a Bournemouth midfielder is Josh’s leading transfer idea, while Calafiori to Marcos Senesi could justify a four-point hit for the Bench Boost.
Calafiori is a notable rotation concern, but managers are advised to start him if they have a strong first substitute because he may not be used off the bench if he does not start.
Kudus, Kinsky and Van de Ven gain appeal after Tottenham’s third straight win, with Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham following the Leeds fixture.
Jackson remains a good Villa forward for the fixture run but is nominated as a possible Gameweek 10 flop away at Manchester United.
Tavernier is an attractive Bournemouth target against Ipswich but carries the risk of chasing recent points and an early substitution.
Eze, Barcola, Isak, Branthwaite and Lewis Hall are highlighted as lower-owned Gameweek 10 differential options.

items.headline: Haaland remains captain as FPL managers weigh up the Jackson bandwagon
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the preferred captain for Gameweek 9 despite Manchester City facing Brighton, with his record against the Seagulls — returns in six of seven meetings, including an assist in the one match he does not score — outweighing Brighton boss Fabian Hürzeler’s unbeaten league record against City. Cole Palmer is the leading alternative at home to Manchester United after serving his suspension in the League Cup, but Haaland is the clear first choice. Nicolas Jackson is a viable differential captain against Fulham, although the recommendation is not to chase that route over Haaland.

Jackson is the dominant transfer of the week after his brace against Manchester City and multiple price rises, with effective ownership expected to become a major rank risk. However, buying him is not automatic for teams with more urgent issues. The preferred move is Malick Thiaw to Bournemouth’s Silva, rather than João Pedro to Jackson, because Thiaw has been benched and could remain a longer-term minutes problem. Silva is viewed as close to a season keeper thanks to Bournemouth’s extended fixture run, while João Pedro’s absence is treated as temporary and Gross can autosub in this week.

Jackson remains an attractive option after the international break, when Aston Villa’s run includes Sunderland at home, Ipswich away, Everton at home and Crystal Palace at home. Unai Emery indicates that Jackson and Manzambi should be available for Fulham despite missing training, but Jackson’s immediate appeal has to be balanced against Villa’s busy schedule, possible European rotation and the opportunity cost of tying up funds in attack. Cheaper forwards such as Thierno Barry, Evanilson and Dominic Calvert-Lewin offer routes to preserve money for Arsenal defender Gabriel, who is considered a major long-term target once Arsenal’s fixtures improve and Aston Villa’s Konsa eventually loses his place to William Saliba.

Barry is narrowly preferred over Evanilson and Calvert-Lewin as the cheaper forward option: he ranks second in the league behind Haaland for expected goal involvement and expected goals, and follows a goal and assist against Newcastle in the League Cup with Newcastle away and Coventry at home next. Evanilson is also in form and has the better immediate fixture case, while Calvert-Lewin is a plausible João Pedro replacement around Gameweek 10 or 12. The broader strategy is to avoid unnecessary hits, retain flexibility through the international break and not make a knowingly inferior transfer simply to match Jackson’s ownership.

For selection calls, Silva, Van Hecke and Mendy are favoured over Konsa, with Mendy expected to return after training and offering strong defensive-contribution potential against Ipswich. Konsa is only marginally ahead of Riccardo Calafiori, whose attacking upside is offset by fitness and minutes uncertainty away to Liverpool. City leaks suggest Foden and Cherki are benched while Haaland, Doku, Dias and Gvardiol start, but the information carries a warning: Manchester City are reportedly aware of early leaks and could alter plans to expose the source.
key_points: Captain Haaland over Palmer and Jackson for Gameweek 9, with Palmer the strongest alternative against Manchester United.
Sell Malick Thiaw for Bournemouth’s Silva rather than forcing João Pedro to Jackson, especially with only one free transfer.
Jackson is a major ownership threat but can still be bought after the break for Villa’s strong Gameweek 11-15 fixture run.
Keep João Pedro where possible this week, allow Gross to autosub, and reassess a switch to Calvert-Lewin or another forward later.
Barry is the preferred budget striker over Evanilson and Calvert-Lewin because of elite underlying numbers, low price and upcoming Newcastle and Coventry fixtures.
Mendy is expected to start against Ipswich after positive training comments; start him ahead of Konsa or De Cuyper in close bench decisions.
Avoid hits for marginal defender upgrades or to remove playable assets, with several Gameweek 9 defensive calls too close to justify a minus four.
Treat reports of Foden and Cherki being benched cautiously, despite leaks naming Haaland, Doku, Dias and Gvardiol as starters.

items.headline: Silva replaces Thomas as Haaland remains the clear Gameweek 9 captain
items.summary:
The key transfer is Thomas to Silva, strengthening a defence built around players with defensive-contribution potential, reliable minutes, solid clean-sheet prospects and some attacking threat. Silva is preferred as a long-term Bournemouth option over more expensive defenders such as Gabriel, while Van Hecke is also endorsed for managers prioritising the immediate fixture. The view is that FPL managers have little value in premium attackers at present, so spending budget on a playable bench and dependable defenders is a valid strategy.

The starting decision is Gross over Sharda. Gross offers penalties, set pieces and dependable 90-minute potential, whereas Sharda carries greater upside but comes with concerns over form, fitness and minutes after an early substitution in Gameweek 8. Sharda is not an urgent sale because the squad can cover him, but he is a likely future exit around Gameweek 11 unless his role improves. Barry ranks highly among forward options and starts ahead of Gross, while Jackson is the preferred Joao Pedro replacement despite unsubstantiated pre-deadline concern over his absence from some training pictures.

Haaland is the overwhelming captain choice for Gameweek 9, with Palmer the vice-captain. Palmer has a strong fixture against Manchester United and remains far too good to bench, but Haaland is considered the safer armband choice. Rogers and Jackson are acceptable differential captain alternatives, while Tavanier captaincy is viewed as unnecessarily ambitious against a Leeds side with a strong defensive record.

A Free Hit is rejected because two free transfers solve the squad’s immediate problems. Gameweek 12, when Arsenal play Manchester City, remains a possible Free Hit window, but it is not yet compelling enough to commit. For managers already using the chip in Gameweek 9, the preferred structure includes Haaland, Palmer, Rogers, Jackson, Barry, Pedro Porro, Van Hecke, Silva and Tavanier, with Ryan a viable short-term alternative to Tavanier. A reported Manchester City leak suggests Foden and Cherki are benched while Gvardiol starts, so Cherki owners are advised to use the information cautiously but plan as though he may not start.
key_points: Transfer Thomas to Silva, with Silva viewed as a rapidly emerging long-term Bournemouth defensive pick.
Start Gross over Sharda because Gross has penalties, set pieces and stronger minute security; Sharda remains benchable rather than an urgent sale.
Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9 and vice-captain Palmer; Palmer is a strong play against Manchester United but not the preferred armband.
Jackson is the leading Joao Pedro replacement, ahead of Barry, Calvert-Lewin and Evanilson; missing training photos do not constitute reliable injury news.
Avoid defender hits in Gameweek 9, with managers encouraged to start available options such as Calafiori, Thomas or De Cuyper instead.
Reported Manchester City team news has Foden and Cherki on the bench and Gvardiol starting, although leaks are never certain.
Do not use the Free Hit merely to solve short-term injuries when transfers can cover them; Gameweek 12 remains under consideration but is not confirmed.
Van Hecke is preferred for immediate fixture appeal, while Silva is preferred as the more reliable every-week defensive hold.

items.headline: Jackson Transfer Carries Late Fitness Risk as Haaland Remains the GW9 Captain
items.summary:
Gameweek 9 arrives with Erling Haaland as the clear captaincy choice, despite a difficult-looking slate of fixtures and widespread uncertainty over team news. Cole Palmer takes the vice-captaincy rather than new signing Nicolas Jackson, while Chelsea’s attacking outlook looks far less convincing without the injured Joao Pedro. Palmer and Morgan Gibbs-White are both under pressure after disappointing runs, but neither is sold immediately because the available replacements and fixtures do not make a compelling short-term case.

The main transfer is Gonzalo Garcia to Jackson, but late concerns emerge after Jackson is absent from Aston Villa training pictures and Villa’s win odds shorten. Unai Emery’s comments do not confirm an injury, so Jackson remains in the squad, but managers yet to buy him are advised to avoid the risk and consider Evanilson instead. Evanilson is not viewed as a standout one-week pick against Leeds, yet Bournemouth’s upcoming fixture run makes him an attractive medium-term forward. Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alexander Isak are also viable alternatives, with Isak offering stronger long-term upside if the budget does not damage the rest of the squad.

Joao Pedro is ruled out for a few weeks but is held with only one free transfer, as he is expected to have a chance of returning after the international break and would likely need buying back. The alternative considered is a -8 to sell Gibbs-White for Bournemouth midfielder Antoine Semenyo or Tavernier/Ryan and upgrade Slater to Manzambi. That move would improve depth and cover Pedro’s absence, but it is rejected because it depends on a hit paying off immediately, while Calafiori’s return to Arsenal training means Slater does not have to start. A hit may become more appealing in Gameweek 10 if Palmer or Gibbs-White continue to underperform and the extra money can be redistributed into Bournemouth assets.

Bournemouth midfielders are the priority attacking targets for the coming weeks. Tavernier is the safer, more rounded selection because of his chance creation and bonus-point potential, while Ryan is a high-upside differential with exceptional recent shot volume, although poor finishing and limited bonus potential make him riskier. Manzambi has appeal as a cheap enabler but carries minutes concerns. In defence, Calafiori is preferred to Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa if Arsenal’s training update is trusted, while Lewis Hall and Egan are strong starts. Double Arsenal defence is acceptable, but a triple-up is considered excessive against Liverpool; Djed Spence/Diker-type defenders facing Manchester City are generally benchable unless squad injuries force them in.

A Free Hit is considered but held back, as the best one-week selections — Bournemouth, Aston Villa and Spurs defensive assets — are also players managers want to own beyond Gameweek 9. Gameweek 15 is earmarked as a more plausible Free Hit window because Bournemouth visit Arsenal, Chelsea face Manchester City and Leeds travel to Liverpool. The immediate aim is to survive Gameweek 9 without further hits, then use the international break and Bournemouth’s Gameweek 10 trip to Ipswich to rebuild squad depth and restore flexibility.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9, with Palmer preferred as vice-captain over Jackson because of late Aston Villa fitness concerns.
Gonzalo Garcia is sold for Nicolas Jackson, but managers who have not moved yet should favour Evanilson if they want to avoid Jackson’s possible injury risk.
Joao Pedro is held despite being out for a few weeks because he may return after the international break and there is only one free transfer available.
A proposed -8 involving Gibbs-White to a Bournemouth midfielder and Slater to Manzambi is rejected, although a restructuring hit in Gameweek 10 remains possible.
Tavernier is the safer Bournemouth midfield pick for creativity and bonus, while Ryan is the higher-risk differential because of his elite shot volume.
Calafiori trains with Arsenal and is preferred to Konsa if starting security is trusted, but avoid a triple Arsenal defensive stack against Liverpool.
Evanilson is the preferred forward alternative to Jackson and is a strong medium-term buy ahead of Bournemouth’s favourable run.
Gameweek 15 is the early Free Hit target, with Bournemouth at Arsenal, Chelsea against Manchester City and Leeds at Liverpool.

items.title: Transfer made 🔒 2 left 🤔 FPL Gameweek 9 Deadline Stream 🚀
items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 9 captain as Jackson fitness doubts cloud Villa transfer plans
items.summary:
Erling Haaland is the standout Gameweek 9 captain despite Brighton’s strong form. Manchester City still carry the league’s most potent attack and Haaland remains the highest-upside option, while alternatives such as Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Antoine Semenyo lack either the fixture, form or certainty to justify a major captaincy gamble. A differential captain is better saved for a week in which Haaland has a genuinely difficult fixture and another premium has a clear favourable matchup.

Nicholas Jackson remains a high-upside replacement for Joao Pedro, but the move carries late uncertainty. Unai Emery says Jackson and Amadou Onana/Manzambi missed the Bournemouth cup tie for “different reasons, not only rest” and should normally play Fulham, yet Jackson is absent from selected training images and Aston Villa’s projected-goal markets shorten amid the speculation. The expectation remains that Jackson starts against Fulham, but managers selling a fit starter may reasonably avoid the risk. If Jackson is already owned, he is worth holding; if confirmed absent, upgrading a cheap midfielder such as Sangare to Marcus Tavernier is preferable to panicking into another striker move.

Defence produces the major selection dilemma. Riccardo Calafiori trains after his recent flag and has greater attacking upside than Ezri Konsa, but there is a meaningful risk of reduced minutes or a substitute appearance against Liverpool. Konsa is the safer pick because he is certain to start, can collect defensive-contribution points and offers set-piece threat. Calafiori is the upside play if managers accept the risk; Konsa is the sensible choice for those protecting a score. Arsenal defenders are not automatic starts away to Liverpool, even with decent clean-sheet odds, and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, Bournemouth options such as Marcos Senesi/James Hill, and Brighton’s Jan Paul van Hecke are viable alternatives depending on budget and fixture horizon.

Most teams are best served by rolling transfers rather than chasing marginal upgrades. Tavernier is an attractive medium-term buy, but moving a playable midfielder such as Morgan Gibbs-White, Harvey Barnes or Pascal Gross solely to fund him is not essential. Gross is usually the expendable bench option in crowded midfields because Manchester City away is difficult, although his penalties and secure minutes keep him viable. Evanilson is preferred to Dominic Calvert-Lewin when a forward must start regularly over the next few weeks, while Calvert-Lewin is useful if his tougher fixtures can be benched. Reports that Phil Foden and Rayan Cherki are benched increase the appeal of City wingers Jeremy Doku and Oscar Bobb/Savio only as short-term punts, not as reliable long-term picks.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 9; Brighton are capable opponents, but City’s attack and Haaland’s ceiling still outweigh the available alternatives.
Jackson is expected to start against Fulham but carries enough late fitness and rotation uncertainty that new buyers should assess their bench strength before moving from Joao Pedro.
Hold Jackson if already owned rather than selling on speculation; if he is definitively ruled out, a Sangare-to-Tavernier type upgrade is a logical contingency.
Start Calafiori only if willing to accept a minutes risk against Liverpool; Konsa is the safer selection through guaranteed starts, defensive-contribution potential and set-piece threat.
Avoid using a free hit primarily to remove Arsenal defenders for Liverpool away unless the wider squad has multiple serious problems.
Tavernier is a good longer-term target, but managers with playable midfields can roll and reassess after the international break.
Evanilson is the stronger forward for sustained starts across the next few gameweeks, while Calvert-Lewin works better as a fixture-dependent rotation option.
Treat reports of Foden and Cherki being benched as a reason to avoid them this week; Doku is a viable short-term differential but remains a Manchester City minutes risk.
